Tool.faq1Q: Are files uploaded to a server?
Tool.faq1A: No. Everything is compressed locally in your browser; files are never uploaded to any server.
Tool.faq2A: This tool compresses common formats including images, PDF, video and audio. See the page for details.
Tool.faq3Q: Why does the first use take time?
Tool.faq3A: Compression engines are WebAssembly modules loaded on demand. The first use downloads the engine (tens of MB); afterwards it is cached locally and needs no re-download.
Tool.faq-image-1A: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF and SVG. JPG is re-encoded with MozJPEG for 80%+ savings; SVG is cleaned with SVGO; PNG is losslessly optimized.
Tool.faq-image-2A: It depends on the level: Maximum gives the smallest size (lossy), Recommended balances size and quality, High is near-lossless. You can also set a target size and the tool auto-searches the closest level.
Tool.faq-image-3A: Yes. We use gifsicle lossy mode to re-quantize the palette, shrinking the file while keeping the animation.
Tool.faq-pdf-1Q: Will PDF compression damage the content?
Tool.faq-pdf-1A: No. We use structural compression that only downsamples embedded images; text and vectors stay untouched. If there are no compressible images it falls back to Ghostscript re-encoding.
Tool.faq-pdf-2Q: How much can scanned PDFs be reduced?
Tool.faq-pdf-2A: Scanned PDFs are almost all image data, so structural compression typically saves 80%–90%+ with no visible difference.
Tool.faq-pdf-3A: Encrypted PDFs cannot be parsed directly; we try re-encoding and show a clear message if it still fails, never producing a broken file.
Tool.faq-video-1Q: How is the quality after video compression?
Tool.faq-video-1A: We re-encode with browser hardware encoding (WebCodecs). At similar quality, size usually drops 60%–80%, fast and without maxing out your CPU.
Tool.faq-video-2A: MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, plus FLV, 3GP, OGV. The first four use hardware encoding; the last three are handled by an FFmpeg fallback that converts to H.264 MP4.
Tool.faq-video-3Q: Why doesn't the video get uploaded?
Tool.faq-video-3A: All video encoding happens locally in your browser; files never leave your device, which is ideal for sensitive or large footage.
Tool.faq-audio-1A: MP3, OGG, AAC, WMA. AAC/OGG use native browser encoders; MP3/WMA are re-encoded to a lower-bitrate MP3 by an FFmpeg fallback.
Tool.faq-audio-2A: Audio is lossy; we shrink the file by lowering the bitrate. High-bitrate sources compressed at Recommended are barely distinguishable.
Tool.faq-audio-3A: Browsers have no built-in MP3 encoder, so MP3 goes through FFmpeg. OGG/AAC have native encoders and use the WebCodecs hardware path.
Tool.faq-zip-1A: Both: it gathers multiple files into one archive while shrinking the total size with a compression algorithm. Everything runs locally.
Tool.faq-zip-2A: Yes. Click 'Choose folder' to recursively collect all files inside; duplicate names are deduplicated.
Tool.faq-zip-3Q: Can the generated ZIP be extracted?
Tool.faq-zip-3A: Yes. This tool focuses on compressing and packaging; the output is a standard ZIP that any extractor can open.
Tool.imageConvertDesc: Convert between JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF formats
Tool.unzipDesc: Extract ZIP archives locally in your browser
Tool.fontDesc: Compress TTF/OTF fonts to WOFF2 web font format
Tool.faq-imageConvert-1A: Conversion itself keeps pixels unchanged. But converting to lossy formats like JPG, WebP or AVIF will change quality depending on the level, so keep a backup of the original lossless file.
Tool.faq-imageConvert-2Q: Which formats can I convert between?
Tool.faq-imageConvert-2A: JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF can be converted to each other. Everything runs locally in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
Tool.faq-imageConvert-3Q: Where does the converted file go?
Tool.faq-imageConvert-3A: Files are never uploaded. The result is generated in your browser and saved to your device when you click download.
Tool.faq-unzip-1Q: Do I need to install software to unzip?
Tool.faq-unzip-1A: No. Everything runs locally in your browser, no installation needed and no files are uploaded.
Tool.faq-unzip-2Q: Can it handle ZIP files with Chinese filenames?
Tool.faq-unzip-2A: Yes. UTF-8 encoded filenames are supported and displayed/downloaded correctly.
Tool.faq-unzip-3Q: Will large archives freeze the page?
Tool.faq-unzip-3A: We extract streaming file-by-file to keep memory usage low; process very large archives in batches.
Tool.faq-font-1Q: How much can WOFF2 compression save?
Tool.faq-font-1A: WOFF2 is the web-optimized font format, usually 50%–70% smaller than TTF/OTF with lossless quality.
Tool.faq-font-2A: TTF and OTF files are accepted and converted to WOFF2, ready for @font-face in web pages.
Tool.faq-font-3Q: How do I use the compressed font?
Tool.faq-font-3A: Put the downloaded .woff2 file in your site directory and declare it in CSS with @font-face; browsers load it on demand.
